title: When the Horizon Burns
premise: Ansel Sandoval, a mountain guide blacklisted from Peru and Chile after a disaster he may or may not have caused, leads a small expedition crew that takes only jobs no one else will touch. When his old rival Mara Voss hires them to follow the Río Ceniza upstream to its forbidden source—a glacier valley sealed off after a mining company's cover-up killed eleven people, including Ansel's brother—the crew discovers the 'forbidden' is enforced by hired guns, not law. As they climb, Ansel's fractured memories of the night his brother died begin to reassemble into a truth more damning than his guilt: he didn't cause the disaster; he witnessed it and was paid to forget. In the end, Ansel chooses testimony over invisibility, broadcasting the evidence from the source itself, knowing it will cost him the last country willing to let him in—but buying the dead their names back.
about_author: Ines Lockridge is the pen name of a former river guide who spent a decade leading expeditions through Patagonia before turning to fiction. Her novels are known for terrain so vivid readers check their own boots for mud.

chapters.title: The Weight of Moving On
chapters.summary: Ansel Sandoval's POV. In a border town he can be expelled from any day, Ansel takes inventory of his crew and his debts, establishing the rule that keeps them alive: never stop moving. A letter arrives with no return address. Emotional beat: restless unease beneath practiced calm.

chapters.title: A Name He Buried
chapters.summary: The letter is from Mara Voss, the rival who testified against him years ago, offering triple pay for an unnamed job. Ansel burns it, then can't stop thinking about it. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: old wounds reopening.

chapters.title: Crew of the Unwanted
chapters.summary: Introduce the team through a dangerous bridge repair job: Teo the engineer with a forged passport, Ilsa the medic fleeing a malpractice scandal, and young Pico who idolizes Ansel without knowing why. POV: rotating crew. Emotional beat: found-family warmth.

chapters.title: Mara at the Door
chapters.summary: Mara Voss arrives in person, older and harder, and names the job: the Río Ceniza source. Ansel refuses flatly. She leaves a photograph of the valley on his table. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: cold fury masking fear.

chapters.title: Eleven Names
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Ansel's POV, of the night the Ceniza dam failed—eleven dead, his brother Tomás among them, and Ansel carried out half-drowned with no memory of the final hour. Emotional beat: grief like sediment.

chapters.title: What the Photograph Shows
chapters.summary: Studying the photo, Teo spots survey equipment that shouldn't exist near a sealed site. Someone has been working there recently. The crew votes; even Ansel's refusal loses. POV: Teo. Emotional beat: reluctant commitment.

chapters.title: Downstream First
chapters.summary: The crew begins at the river's mouth, interviewing survivors' families under the guise of a fishing survey. A widow recognizes Ansel and spits at his feet. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: shame made physical.

chapters.title: The Company That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Records show the mining consortium was dissolved on paper, yet its security contractors still patrol the watershed. Ilsa treats a boy injured by a patrol tripwire. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: dawning scale of the cover-up.

chapters.title: Blacklist Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Ansel calculates what taking this job costs: both remaining countries will expel him if discovered. He almost walks away, then finds Mara's second letter—she knows about the missing hour of his memory. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: cornered.

chapters.title: Upstream Begins
chapters.summary: The crew launches boats into the Ceniza gorge, leaving vehicles and identities behind. First contact with a patrol drone forces them to travel by night. POV: Pico. Emotional beat: exhilaration curdling to dread.

chapters.title: Rapids and Reckonings
chapters.summary: A Class V rapid nearly swamps the lead boat; Ansel's legendary skill saves Pico but exposes how much risk he'll take with others' lives. Teo confronts him privately. POV: Teo. Emotional beat: trust cracking.

chapters.title: The Village That Was Moved
chapters.summary: They find a resettlement village built to house the displaced—half empty, watched, its residents afraid to speak. An old fisherman draws them a map in exchange for medicine. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: quiet complicity of survival.

chapters.title: Mara's Version
chapters.summary: Mara rejoins the expedition upstream and tells her side: she testified against Ansel because the evidence pointed there, but she's spent ten years doubting it. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: rivalry softening into alliance.

chapters.title: First Blood
chapters.summary: A patrol ambush kills their radio and wounds Teo. Ilsa operates by headlamp while Ansel holds him down. They realize the patrols aren't guarding the valley—they're guarding something being destroyed inside it. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: terror sharpening resolve.

chapters.title: The Missing Hour
chapters.summary: Hypoxia-like fragments surface as Ansel sleeps at altitude: a flashlight, a voice saying 'sign it,' Tomás shouting. He wakes screaming. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: memory as ambush.

chapters.title: Portage Through Hell
chapters.summary: The river enters a canyon too violent to boat; five days hauling gear over scree. Pico saves Ansel from a rockfall, reversing their debt. POV: Pico. Emotional beat: loyalty cemented in sweat.

chapters.title: The Checkpoint
chapters.summary: A fortified checkpoint blocks the last navigable stretch. Mara proposes a diversion using her own name as bait—she's been arrested there before and released, meaning someone protects her. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: sacrifice offered.

chapters.title: Ghosts in the Fog
chapters.summary: While Mara distracts the checkpoint, the others portage past—and Ansel sees a figure on the ridge wearing Tomás's jacket. It vanishes. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: grief weaponized against him.

chapters.title: Interrogation of One
chapters.summary: Mara, detained, is questioned by a contractor named Reyes who reveals the operation above: they're demolishing the dam ruins and everything buried beneath them. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: clock now audible.

chapters.title: Above the Treeline
chapters.summary: The crew climbs out of the gorge onto glacial moraine. Altitude sickness fells Ilsa; they shelter in an abandoned survey hut full of documents the company missed. POV: Teo. Emotional beat: hope with frostbite.

chapters.title: Documents in the Hut
chapters.summary: The surveys prove the dam was deliberately overtopped to destroy records of toxic tailings leakage—an engineered disaster. Eleven people were inconvenient. POV: Teo. Emotional beat: rage going cold and precise.

chapters.title: Why Ansel Survived
chapters.summary: Cross-referencing, Teo realizes Ansel was pulled from the water downstream of where anyone could swim—he was dumped. Someone wanted him alive. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: the ground of his identity tilting.

chapters.title: The Voice Saying Sign It
chapters.summary: Ansel finally recalls: company men found him half-conscious and forced his thumbprint on a false incident report—the basis of his blacklist. His disgrace was manufactured twice over. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: vindication arriving too heavy to carry.

chapters.title: Rescue or Recapture
chapters.summary: Mara escapes detention with help from an unexpected ally: a patrol guard whose father died in the flood. She reaches the high camp wounded. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: enemies becoming kin.

chapters.title: The Glacier Wall
chapters.summary: The source lies beyond an icefall. They rope up and climb through a storm, Pico leading where Ansel hesitates—his memory of the icefall is why he survived, and it terrifies him. POV: Pico. Emotional beat: courage passed down.

chapters.title: Tomás's Cache
chapters.summary: In a crevasse shelter, they find supplies cached a decade ago—Tomás reached the source first and hid evidence here, then died trying to bring it out. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: his brother ahead of him all along.

chapters.title: The Source
chapters.summary: They reach the forbidden valley: a meltwater lake beneath the glacier, ringed by demolition crews erasing the ruin. The evidence cache is half-buried in fresh blast debris. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: awe and violation in one breath.

chapters.title: Reyes Closes In
chapters.summary: Reyes's teams sweep the valley. The crew splits: some carry the documents toward the satellite uplink point, while Ansel draws pursuit. POV: Teo. Emotional beat: the plan fraying at speed.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Moraine
chapters.summary: Teo is captured; Ilsa and Pico escape with the core evidence. Reyes offers Ansel a trade: Teo for the documents and their silence—the same bargain he accepted ten years ago. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: history offering a rerun.

chapters.title: The Bargain Refused
chapters.summary: Ansel says no—but not the way he did before. He negotiates time, stalls Reyes, and signals Mara. For the first time he fights with a plan instead of panic. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: the man who runs choosing to stand.

chapters.title: Prisoner Exchange
chapters.summary: Mara's guard-ally turns his patrol's weapons on Reyes's men; in the chaos the crew frees Teo, though the guard is killed covering their retreat. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: cost written in a stranger's blood.

chapters.title: Demolition Day
chapters.summary: The company accelerates the demolition to bury everything tomorrow—including, Reyes decides, the witnesses. The crew has one night. POV: Teo. Emotional beat: deadline as drumbeat.

chapters.title: Into the Ice Cave
chapters.summary: Ansel realizes the deepest evidence—Tomás's original recordings—is inside the glacier cave beneath the dam ruin, scheduled to collapse. He goes in alone. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: descending into his own past literally.

chapters.title: His Brother's Voice
chapters.summary: In the cave, Ansel finds Tomás's recorder: footage of the sabotage order, and a message naming Ansel as the one person Tomás trusted to finish it. The charges detonate early; the cave begins to fail. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: love delivered posthumously.

chapters.title: Collapse
chapters.summary: Ansel races the collapsing ice, nearly dies in a crevasse fall, and is hauled out by Pico and Ilsa as the dam ruin vanishes behind them—with Reyes believing every trace destroyed. POV: Pico. Emotional beat: resurrection by friendship.

chapters.title: The Uplink
chapters.summary: At the ridge station, they broadcast the recordings, the surveys, and Ansel's sworn testimony to every press outlet and court that will receive it. Reyes's men arrive shooting. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: truth leaving their hands forever.

chapters.title: Standoff at the Source
chapters.summary: Cornered above the new lake, the crew makes its last stand until the broadcast goes confirmed-live; Reyes's own contractors, seeing their orders exposed, stand down and arrest him. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: justice arriving sideways, outside any courtroom.

chapters.title: Names Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Weeks later, at a memorial the company can no longer erase, the eleven names are read publicly. Ansel speaks Tomás's aloud himself. Warrants against him dissolve; the blacklist becomes testimony. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: grief given a public shape.

chapters.title: What Stopping Costs
chapters.summary: Ansel faces the paradox he feared: staying still, being seen, being known. Mara offers him partnership in a legitimate guiding outfit; Pico asks to stay on. He unpacks a bag for the first time in a decade. POV: Ansel. Emotional beat: stillness as the hardest summit.

chapters.title: When the Horizon Burns
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Ansel's POV. At dawn on a ridge above the restored Ceniza valley, the sunrise sets the glacier burning gold. He no longer needs to outrun the light. The river runs clear. Emotional beat: arrival—not at a place, but at himself.
